article_text:
The gulf between the safe and loving world that we want to make for children and the world that we live in is vaster than a galaxy. But in “ Josephine, ” Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan are parents forced to navigate that void when, on an otherwise unremarkable Saturday morning, their daughter Josephine (newcomer Mason Reeves) witnesses an assault in the San Francisco park where they like to jog.

The inciting incident is loosely based on something that actually happened to writer and director Beth de Araújo when she was young. But the place that she, and the film , take the fallout from this event is unique to the filmmaker’s uncanny ability to explore how power and evil move so freely in our world, both when people have terrible intentions and when their intentions are good.

As IndieWire’s Kate Erbland wrote in her review , “Araújo remains undefeated when it comes to making stunning films that I will both heartily recommend and never, ever watch again. The word that comes to mind when watching a Araújo feature is heartsick. That applies to the feeling bestowed on both the audience and her characters (the good guys and the bad guys). While her first film, the unrelenting ‘Soft & Quiet,’ was cleverly designed to appear as if it was shot in a single real-time take, her sophomore feature is more about the steady accumulation of dread.”

“Josephine” first premiered at Sundance, and has made the festival circuit this fall to great acclaim. At TIFF , Araújo spoke to IndieWire about how the film has been a slow, stop-start process from a first draft in 2014 to an important 2018 revision as part of that year’s Sundance Labs, to working with Tatum and Chan and casting Reeves, only six weeks out from shooting. But the young breakout star of the film, who is from the same part of San Francisco that Araújo grew up in, was meant to be.

“I think everyone felt a real responsibility to make sure Mason had a good experience,” Araújo told IndieWire. “And I think that bonded us all as cast and crew. It’s like, there’s something more innocent than us here.”

“Josephine” releases in theaters on Friday, November 20. Watch the film’s latest trailer below.

article_text:
Josh Brolin can now add a different kind of role to his resume.

In addition to starring as Mitt Gardiner, the late father of Austin Abrams’ character Jay in “ Whalefall ,” aspects of the actor were also used to create the appearance of the sperm whale that traps Jay inside its body for the majority of the film.

As Jay fights for survival, he communicates with the spirit of his father (via Brolin’s voice), which also doubles as the spirit of the whale. Because the its heartbeat triggers a specific lighting effect throughout the film, director Brian Duffield revealed they recorded Brolin’s heartbeat and doubled it for the whale’s, further solidifying the late father’s affinity and connection with the mammal.

“We obviously don’t have a native sperm whale heartbeat recorded,” Duffield told Variety at the film’s premiere on Tuesday. “It just became like, ‘Well, we need to get a heartbeat. Where do we get the heartbeat?’ And then it was, ‘We have Josh!’”

Brolin also inspired the physical appearance of the whale, Duffield revealed at the premiere, which was held at the El Capitan Theatre. In an attempt to visually tie the two together, creatives gave the whale similar facial scarring to Brolin’s character. It was a subliminal choice, Duffield said, but it was enough to mean something to both Abrams and the filmmakers.

“It’s just whatever you can do to make it feel as personal as possible,” the director said. “Even if it’s something that no one will notice.”

“Whalefall” is one of three films featuring Brolin this year, including the third installment of the “Dune” franchise set to release Dec. 18. While promoting “Whalefall,” Brolin told Variety he’s happy that theatrical releases have seen a jump at the box office, including for the re-release of “Avengers: Endgame,” which he “didn’t even know” recently returned to the big screen.

“Going to the theaters on Sundays when I was in my early 20s and my late teens, and the lights would go down — it was just a heart-opening experience that I never wanted to let go,” Brolin said.

However, Brolin’s Ridley Scott-directed “The Dog Stars,” earned just $8 million domestically its opening weekend in August. the actor said he wasn’t fazed by the numbers as it’s impossible to know “what’s going to work.”

“‘Dog Stars’ did an incredible marketing campaign, and then nobody saw it,” he said, also noting that box office failures can eventually find success via streaming.

Brolin recalled his 2017 film “Only the Brave,” which initially bombed at box offices but later became a streaming hit. “You don’t know if you’re going to be part of the zeitgeist or not,” he said.

article_text:
“ MobLand ” actor Mandeep Dhillon has started production on short “The Things I Want to Do to You,” which she wrote and will star in.

Directed by BAFTA nominee Lynette Linton, the psychological drama also features “Bridgerton” star Golda Rosheuvel and “The Game’s” Scott Karim. It’s produced by Katie Glaister under Dhillon’s production banner Hazy Plant Pictures Ltd., marking the company’s first project.

“The Things I Want to Do to You” explores “rage, revenge, trauma and the complexities of seeking justice,” according to its official synopsis. The short film “follows a woman navigating the aftermath of a deeply personal violation. Through a series of increasingly provocative fantasies, she confronts the things she wishes she could do to the man responsible. Blurring the lines between imagination and reality, the film examines the anger women are often forced to carry in silence and what happens when that anger finally demands to be heard.”

“I’ve always been fascinated by the things we think but never say out loud, particularly when we’ve been wronged,” Dhillon said in a statement. “The anger, the grief, the fantasies of revenge and the conversations we have in our heads that will never happen in real life. I think so many women carry the weight of injustice, often in silence. I wanted to explore that space between what we feel, what we imagine and what we actually do. The darker, sometimes outrageous, places our minds can go when we feel powerless. At its heart, this film is about giving a voice to those unspoken emotions and exploring what it means to carry something you never asked for.”

“The Things I Want to Do to You” is currently filming in the U.K., with other cast members including Arabella Coombes, Eisa Latif and Saher Shah.

Dhillon added, “To be bringing this story to life alongside Lynette Linton, Golda Rosheuvel and such an incredible team is something I’m immensely proud of. As the first production from my company, Hazy Plant Pictures, it feels particularly special, and I couldn’t be more excited for this to mark the beginning of our journey.”

To receive Morning Links in your inbox every weekday, sign up for our Breakfast with ARTnews newsletter.

Good morning!

François Pinault will install a permanent exhibition of 106 works from his collection at Palazzo Grassi, one of his two museums in Venice.

The Louvre’s security coordinator said the museum is accelerating a “culture of safety and security.”

An inspection has uncovered that the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool liner failed in at least 85 places, far more than previously was known, due to a rushed renovation job.

The Headlines

THE SHOW MUST GO ON. Kering founder and Christie’s owner François Pinault plans to install a permanent exhibition of 106 works from his collection in Palazzo Grassi , one of his two museums in Venice, he told Le Monde . In the interview, he also discussed why he collects and what sparks his attention. “My collection is eminently subjective and very often built on instinct, passion, or even anger in the face of the violence of the present,” he said. He also explained that after years of temporary exhibitions, which give a more fleeting sense of his collection, numbering over 10,000 artworks, a permanent display would allow visitors to fully experience more of the works that have deeply marked him over the years. “A permanent display makes it possible to set works from different periods and generations side by side and to show how … certain questions endure. It is in no way a matter of freezing the collection or offering a definitive reading of it,” he added.

LOUVRE’S TOP COP . Olivier Goupil , a former police commissioner who is now in charge of security at the Louvre in Paris, gave an update to Le Figaro on the beleaguered museum’s current systems and how he is accelerating a “culture of safety and security” at the institution. This ranges from new cameras and detective devices on artworks, to new security checks at entrances. “Everything is urgent, but everything is moving forward,” he said.

The Digest

An inspection report commissioned in August uncovered that the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool liner failed in at least 85 places, far more than previously was known, due to a rushed renovation job and the use of improper materials, with no mention of any harm done by vandalism. [ The Washington Post ]

Artists say they feel silenced by new laws in Turkey prohibiting the depiction of LGBTQI+ symbols in art and culture, including the rainbow. [ Taz Newspaper ]

Artists are in a pinch after learning that a key material used in sculpture-making, called Hydrocal plaster, will no longer be produced by its main supplier, the USG Corporation in Blaine County, Oklahoma. [ The New York Times ]

A previously unknown Canaletto pen and ink drawing dated to 1746 to 1755, depicting an overgrown arcade in ruins, has surfaced and is heading to auction at Mallams in the UK on October 21, for a high estimate of $79,000. [ Artnet News ]

Mexico’s military is putting plans on hold for a massive military museum complex that was proposed for Mexico City, and within part of the beloved Bosque de Chapultepec park. [ The Art Newspaper ]

The Kicker

SEEING RED . Writing for the Financial Times , reporter Melanie Gerlis visits several red-voting “flyover” states, taking the pulse of what she says are buzzing arts scenes that have attracted a rising cohort of creative talent and market pros. They have recently been joined by the Ostillo Art Foundation in Austin, Texas, a nonprofit backed by collector René Campos that opened last month and is free. Nearby in Houston, “market activity is stepping up,” writes Gerlis, who spoke to Michael Slenske , director of the young Untitled Art, Houston fair, about the city’s philanthropic culture and growing number of established artists moving in, like Rick Lowe, Mark Flood , and JooYoung Choi . Slenske said Houston has “a rising tide of [cultural] ambition.” This tracks with feedback from Atlanta, where Kelly Freeman of fair producer Art Market Production says: “If you want to be part of the community, there are so many people excited to talk to you. It’s not exclusionary, it’s ‘come on in and learn.’”

article_text:
Im Männerzirkel um Joseph Beuys war Katharina Sieverding eine der wenigen Studentinnen. Nun tritt ihr Werk auf Schloss Moyland in einen Dialog mit ihrem ehemaligen Lehrer. Zum Glück verzichtet die Schau auf klassische Schüler-Meister-Muster

"Jetzt ist Schluss mit High Culture. Jetzt gehe ich zu Beuys, jetzt möchte ich meine eigenen Statements formulieren." Mit diesen Worten verabschiedete sich die Künstlerin Katharina Sieverding 1967 von ihrer Arbeit als Kostüm- und Bühnenbildnerin und aus der Klasse von Teo Otto an der Kunsthochschule Düsseldorf. Der Entschluss hatte sich bei einer Hauptprobe der "Zauberflöte" bei den Salzburger Festspielen angebahnt. Als eine Tür klemmte, die Sarastro für seinen Abgang öffnen sollte, geriet der Dirigent völlig aus der Fassung und Sieverding ärgerte sich. Nicht nur über die Theatralik um ein störrisches Objekt, sondern vor allem über das, was sie in diesem Moment in der Welt der Bühne sah: einen zu begrenzten Handlungsraum.

Einen Tag vorher war der Student Benno Ohnesorg bei einer Demonstration gegen den Besuch des Schahs von Persien von einem Polizisten erschossen worden. Während sich auf der Bühne alles um eine klemmende Tür drehte, war draußen etwas geschehen, das für Sieverding eine grundsätzliche Frage aufwarf: Wie kann Kunst auf eine solche Gegenwart reagieren? In der Düsseldorfer Klasse des "Konzeptpapstes" Joseph Beuys sah sie fruchtbaren Boden für die Suche nach einer Antwort.

Eine Ausstellung im Museum Schloss Moyland setzt Katharina Sieverding nun in einen Dialog mit ihrem ehemaligen Lehrer. Dass die Künstlerin ursprünglich vom Theater kommt, ist dabei mehr als eine biografische Fußnote. Schon im Treppenhaus beginnt die Schau mit einer Szene: Eine hochformatige, überlebensgroße Fotoarbeit von Sieverding mit dem Schriftzug "Love and Peace from Katharina" (1972) tritt Joseph Beuys' ebenso großem Bild "We Are the Revolution (La Rivoluzione siamo Noi)" aus demselben Jahr gegenüber.

Beuys tritt in Sieverdings Bildraum ein

Beide Werke zeigen jeweils ihre Urheberin und ihren Urheber, wie sie auf die Betrachtenden zugehen. Zwei Arbeiten, zwei Gesichter, zwei künstlerische Selbstbehauptungen. Man könnte darin ein Blickduell sehen. Oder eine mögliche Rivalität. Aber vielmehr stimmt diese Anordnung direkt auf die Idee der Ausstellung ein: Nicht Sieverding wird hier über ihre Nähe zu Beuys erklärt. Vielmehr tritt Beuys in ihren Bildraum ein und erscheint darin mitunter überraschend anders.

Dass die Kunstwelt Katharina Sieverding fast an die Bretter verloren hätte, die die Welt bedeuten, betont die Ausstellung in der Werkauswahl. Erstmals wird eine bislang weitestgehend unbekannte Sammlung von Kostüm- und Bühnenbildentwürfen gezeigt.

30 Skizzen beschreiben Sieverdings Ideen für das Theater der Nachkriegszeit von 1963 bis 1967. Dass diese Arbeit auch den Grundstein für ihre spätere künstlerische Beschäftigung mit Kleidung, Auftreten und Inszenierung gelegt haben könnte, liegt nahe.

Beuys wird dramatisch

Die Ausstellung auf Schloss Moyland im nordrhein-westfälischen Bedburg-Hau verzichtet dankenswerterweise auf die vertraute Erzählung vom Meister und seiner Schülerin. Sieverding steht im Mittelpunkt, Beuys ist kein bloßer Stichwortgeber, und die Beuys-Sammlung des Schlosses wird zum Resonanzraum für eine Begegnung, die sich nicht in kunsthistorischen Einflusslinien erschöpft. Was verbindet zwei Kunstschaffende, die ähnliche Fragen umtreiben, aber unterschiedliche Herangehensweisen wählen? Und was wird sichtbar, wenn ihre Arbeiten nicht chronologisch oder hierarchisch, sondern im direkten Miteinander betrachtet werden?

"Ich wusste gar nicht, wie dramatisch Beuys doch wirken kann", sagt der Kurator Alexander Grönert und zeigt auf das Werk "Grassello, CA(OH)2 + H2O" von 1981. Gegenüber von Katharina Sieverdings "Grossfoto III/1975" bekommt Beuys' Rückenansicht plötzlich etwas Melancholisches, wie Caspar David Friedrichs "Wanderer über dem Nebelmeer". Fast wie eine Figur auf der Bühne wirkt der "große Beuys" da. Und neben Sieverdings Werkdimension plötzlich auch klein.

"Das Werk habe ich schon so oft ausgestellt, aber wie in dieser Hängung hat es noch nie gewirkt", erzählt Grönert. Er hat die Ausstellung co-kuratiert, gemeinsam mit Antje-Britt Mählmann, der künstlerischen Direktorin des Museums, sowie Katharina Sieverdings Kindern Orson, Musiker und Medienkünstler , und Pola, Film- und Fotokünstlerin . Beide arbeiten im Studio Sieverding und kennen das Werk ihrer Mutter in- und auswendig. Eine solche Schau haben sie aber noch nie gestaltet. "Es war ein sehr kreativer und produktiver Prozess", sagt Grönert.

Es ist genug Raum für alle da

Herausgekommen ist eine Präsentation, die sowohl Katharina Sieverding als auch Joseph Beuys Raum bietet. Dafür verzichtet sie auf klassische Begleittexte. Stattdessen sind immer wieder Zitate der beiden Hauptpersonen zu lesen.

Sieverdings fotografische Praxis geht über Dokumentation hinaus. Zum Beispiel, wenn sie in "Arena Beuys Rom Solarisation 2 & 1" (1972) dessen Aktion "Titus/Iphigenie" auf ihre Art festhält. Ihre Arbeiten sind vergrößert, collagiert, zusammengesetzt, überblendet, neu bearbeitet. In Film und Fotografie verhandelt Sieverding ihre Auseinandersetzung mit der Wirklichkeit.

Während Joseph Beuys seinen Hut zum Markenzeichen gemacht hat, richtet Katharina Sieverding den Blick immer wieder auf das Gesicht, auf ihr eigenes ebenso wie auf das Antlitz als soziale Projektionsfläche. Ihre fotografischen Selbstinszenierungen sind keine klassischen Porträts, sondern fragen, was aus einem Gesicht wird, wenn es Bild ist. Welche Vorstellungen von Macht, Geschlecht, Identität und politischer Haltung schreiben sich darin ein? Was sehen wir tatsächlich, und was tragen wir selbst an Erwartungen an das Bild heran? Dabei wird sowohl bei Beuys als auch bei Sieverding die eigene Erscheinung zum künstlerischen Material.

Dialog heißt nicht, dass man sich einig ist

Für Sieverding ist ein Bild nie einfach nur Abbild: Es ist eine Setzung, ein Statement, eine Form der Intervention. In der "Transformer"-Reihe von 1973/74 verhandelt sie beispielsweise durch Überblendung des Gesichts ihres Partners Klaus Mettig ihre Position in der damaligen feministischen Debatte. Im Dialog mit Beuys treten dabei unerwartete Verbindungen hervor. Beide verstehen Kunst nicht als abgeschlossenen ästhetischen Bereich, sondern als etwas, das in gesellschaftliche Auseinandersetzungen hineinwirkt und Fragen stellt.

Ihre Antworten fallen allerdings unterschiedlich aus. "Ich habe bei der Arbeit für diese Ausstellung neue Ebenen zu Beuys' Werken entdecken können. Das finde ich so spannend daran, sie in den Dialog mit anderen Kunstschaffenden zu setzen", sagt Kurator Grönert. Das Beispiel Sieverding-Beuys zeigt allerdings auch, dass Dialog nicht immer heißen muss, dass man auf einen Nenner kommt.

Umgekehrte Blickrichtung

Zwischen Sieverdings großformatigen Arbeiten an den Wänden der Ausstellungshalle hängen immer wieder elegant eingeschmiegt Zeichnungen von Joseph Beuys. Dass sich Katharina Sieverdings Werk nicht auf die Beziehung zu ihrem Lehrer reduzieren lässt, sollte man an diesem Punkt der Ausstellung schon gespürt haben. Eine (leider) gewohnte Blickrichtung wird hier vielmehr umgekehrt: Katharina Sieverding muss nicht neben Joseph Beuys bestehen, sondern verändert vielleicht sogar hier und da, wie wir den "Meister" sehen.

"Es steht ihm gut, die Werke sehen schick neben ihr aus", resümiert Alexander Grönert beim Verlassen des Museums. Katharina Sieverding und Joseph Beuys sind hier in einen Dialog auf Augenhöhe getreten. Das bedeutet nicht, dass beide gleich aussehen oder dasselbe sagen. Es bedeutet, dass ihre Werke einander etwas entlocken, das sonst vielleicht unsichtbar geblieben wäre.

article_text:
傷の奥に積もる時間

最初に目を引くのは、画面を走る無数の傷である。近づくと、重なる紙の下から、暗い色が透けてくることがわかる。

この作品を作ったのは、1959年にソウルで生まれ、1983年に渡仏した 李鎮雨 （り・じんう）だ。パリ第8大学造形美術学修士、パリ国立高等美術学校を修了し、いまもパリを拠点に制作を続けている。傷に見える線は、炭と韓紙を重ねて擦ったワイヤーブラシの跡だ。何日分もの労働が、一枚の画面に積もっている。

留学先になぜパリを選んだのかを李に尋ねると、 「パリが美術の都市だから行ったというのが、じつは2番目の理由なんです」 という答えが返ってきた。1980年代の韓国は、軍事政権による強権的な支配と、それに対する激しい民主化運動がせめぎ合う激動の時代にあった。貧しさも重なり、美術の勉強を続けられる社会状況ではなかったという。世宗大学で4年間絵画を学んだものの、さらに先へ進むには国を出るほかなかった。そこで、アメリカではなくヨーロッパへ、という思いだけで、ほとんど予備知識のないまま、李は「美術の街」のパリへ旅立った。

パリ第8大学の大学院では3年にわたり研究と論文の執筆に取り組み、現代美術の理論などの授業を受けた。続くパリ国立高等美術学校では、7年間、材料学を学んでいる。学生は材料を自分で作り、使い、その結果を学生同士で議論した。李はこの時間を、 「それ自体が作品の元になっています」 と振り返る。

その学びは、作品のかたちにも表れる。硬く、厚みのある大作に見えても、巻いて運べるものがある。巻けるように作ると決めたものは、それに合わせた作り方で仕上げられているという。長い時間をかけて材料の性質を知り尽くした作家の仕事である。

水が蘇らせたもの

パリで作家として歩み出した李の道のりは、決して平坦ではなかった。29歳の頃、作品が食費になることはなく、暮らしを支えたのは白い豆だった。いちばん安かったのは、インド人の店で買える、年月を経て乾き切った硬い豆で、ほかの種類の3分の1ほどの値段だったという。ただし、水に12時間以上浸けなければ食べられない。ある日、李は豆を水に浸したまま食事に招かれて出かけた。戻ってみると、豆から小さな芽が出ていた。「死んでいたと思っていた豆が、水のおかげで蘇った」。暗く孤独な環境のなかで、その小さな芽は自分を救うように輝いて見えたという。このとき得た「水は生命であり、死んだものを救う」という実感が、李の制作の中心にある「水」の発想の出発点になった。

いっぽう、パリでは同化を求められない代わりに、自分は何者かを繰り返し問われた。教授たちは李に「あなたが韓国人であることの特徴は何か」と尋ね、母国の文化を保ちながら自分のものを作ることを促した。

この問いへの答えを、李は食べ物や衣装や言語ではなく、美術の材料に探した。「韓国人だけが使用する美術材料について探り始めました」と李は語る。西洋美術が独自の材料とともに発展してきたように、韓国の人々もまた数百年をかけて材料の性質を見出してきたはず。こうして油彩を離れ、それまで知らなかった韓紙と炭を、一から学ぶ道を選んだ。どちらもフランスでは入手が難しく、材料のために韓国へ赴いて買い込んだという。以来40年あまり、李は韓紙と炭、そして水を使い続けている。

技法の原点にはまた、留学中に目にした光景がある。ストロンボーリ島の噴火に居合わせた李は、持ち帰った火山灰を作品のモチーフとした。炭と韓紙を何層にも重ねる反復は、自身の「何か」を「頭」や「脳」を介さずに表出するための手段だという。思考の干渉を防ぐ強い労働の反復は、国際的に再評価の機運がある韓国の単色画（ダンセクファ）の「行為の反復」「修行」「精神性」とも重なる。

炭を置いた画面に韓紙を載せ、水を含ませてワイヤーブラシで擦る。乾いたらまた韓紙を重ね、擦る。この繰り返しが1点につき20回以上に及び、紙の層のあいだには毎回水が含まれる。黒い炭は光を吸収し、白い韓紙は光を反射する。相反するふたつの性質を重ねるうちに、最初に置いたレイヤーの色が層の奥から立ち上がってくる。

作品の静けさを支えているのは、体を使う仕事だ。作業台を複数並べ、水に濡らして擦った作品が乾くあいだに、別の作品へ移る。その日々のなかで、手は洗っても落ちない青黒い色に染まり、長年の仕事を物語るように厚みを増している。

いっぽう、「水」をモチーフとする近年の新作では、雨が大きな比重を占める。斜めに流れる作品は、風を受けて降る雨を思わせる。李は学生時代から雨を描きたいと思っていたが、「方法がなかった」という。そこで、以前はキャンバスに絵具を塗って雨の日に外へ置き、雨粒の跡を画面に残す作品を作ったことがあると語った。現存しないその作品への思いが、新しい連作につながった。ワイヤーブラシに加えて細い竹で表面を叩く手法を用い、より柔らかく繊細なリズムで雨を表そうとしたのだ。

紙の外へ、土のほうへ

李と日本の関わりは、日本の戦後美術や韓国・中国の現代美術をいち早く扱い、世界に紹介してきた銀座の 東京画廊＋BTAP での個展を通じて続いてきた。同画廊では、2017年に日本初の個展「森の奥で」が開催され、2021年にも新作を紹介する個展が開かれた。昨年の個展 「潤（윤）」 も、その延長にある。

日本への関心は、いま具体的なかたちになろうとしている。次の一歩となるのは、大塚オーミ陶業との協働だ。大塚国際美術館の運営でも知られる同社は、信楽焼の産地として名高い滋賀・信楽に拠点を持つ。きっかけは、作品のエディションを制作する必要が生じたことにあった。そこで知り合いの陶芸家から同社を勧められ、李は試作のために信楽を訪れた。原本の表面の質感がセラミックで再現されるのを確かめ、複製にとどめるにはもったいない技術だという判断から、現在は新作の制作へと発想が広がっている。

李にとって陶は初めて扱う素材であり、職人と共同で作品を作ることも初めての経験になる。「私が一度も使わなかった材料と、誰かと協力することは初めてなので、新しい変化の機会ができると期待しています」と李は語る。

もうひとつ、李が30年にわたり毎日続けているのが書道である。パリのアトリエの2階で、ひとり筆を持つ。手を使うことを保つための日課であり、書いた上にまた文字を書き重ね、やがてその姿が見えなくなるまで続ける。年を重ね、大作に必要な労働が難しくなったときにも、この書道を続けて残していくことが、李の長期的な目標だという。

画面を走る無数の傷は、最初に置いた炭の暗さを、表面まで引き出すための跡である。李は韓紙を重ね、擦り、作家の考えも技術も見えなくなるまで手を動かす。暗がりのなかで水が豆を蘇らせたあの記憶を、40年あまり、画面で繰り返してきたようにも見える。そして李はいま、新しい素材にも向かい、日本の職人と新作を作ろうとしている。韓紙の層で積み上げてきた時間は、次はでどんな痕跡として表れるか。それを確かめられる日を待ちたい。

2024", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "9. 对莱克而言，身为同性恋是一个母题；他围绕这一主题进行创作，这是他身上一个本质性的、独特的特征，但他正如他自己所说，并不是一个同性恋艺术家，也没有在创作同性恋艺术。将性身份视为一种根本的、内在于己的真理或决定性特征，是对个人的一种无法证实的假设，他所创作的艺术亦是如此。没有人愿意——事实上也无法——背负这种代表性的沉重包袱。这不可避免地会导致人们陷入虚假确定性和虚假普遍性的泥潭之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉姆齐·法瓦兹（Ramzi Fawaz）在《Queer Forms》中试图在身份政治与他所谓的“酷儿流动性（queer fluidity）”的准自由与灵活性之间架起桥梁，然而，如果这种表述剥夺了特定且多元身份的存在空间或不允许其存在，它本身也可能演变成一种规范化的思维模式。与此相反，酷儿形式则是“一种形态的转化。” 6 形态转化生动地展现了个人如何在时间流逝中为自我形象赋予意义并对其进行重塑，同时也展示了当 feminist（女性主义）和酷儿形式被不同的受众采纳并进行解读时，它们如何演变、再次出现或揭示出更多的维度。莱克的艺术可以被视作一种“酷儿形式”。酷儿形式是指任何朝向性别与性少数群体、或包含性别与性不遵从/差异维度的物质形态、结构或模式。与此同时，酷儿形式也展现了性别和性倾向的不同维度，从而使它们能够被我们的感知所捕捉，并引发能够体现性别与性倾向多面维度的诠释。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "通过某种形式——在本例中是以部分带有同性恋形象的陶瓷为载体——可以将性与性别的某个面向可视化并加以讨论，也就是像赖克所体验和遇到的那样，关于同性恋情色以及属于和面向同性恋者的视觉文化的一部分，然后他将其转化为一种新的媒介、一个新的不同的层面。参见例如《无题（塞巴斯蒂安）》（Zonder titel (Sebastiaan)）及旁边的图片。照片中的男子符合许多关于同性恋者“应该长什么样”的刻板印象。非常健硕、毛发旺盛且穿着一条小泳裤。圣塞巴斯蒂安经常被用来描绘男性裸体。这两个世界在这里交汇，以思考对男性裸体和（显而易见的）完美的崇拜。顺着转化与革新的路径，有助于我们避免在潜在的意识形态含义中停留过久，或者避免纠结于“它们在反映性少数群体真实经验方面的所谓真实性”，7而是让我们能够审视那种建立新联系、创造理念与图像的创造力，从而让我们能够继续彼此交谈。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Plat-eendimensionaal-porno-2-1600x1447.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Chris Rijk - Zonder titel (Plat)

In Queer Forms wil Ramzi Fawaz een brug slaan tussen identiteitsdenken en de, volgens hem, quasi vrijheid en flexibiliteit van “ queer fluidity ” dat ook weer als een normatief denkpatroon kan gaan fungeren als door die uitdrukking specifieke en verschillende identiteiten niet kunnen bestaan of geen ruimte krijgen. Queer vormen daarentegen zijn “een soort gedaanteverandering.” 6 Gedaanteverandering illustreert hoe individuen hun zelfbeeld in de loop van de tijd betekenisvol vormgeven en hervormen, en de manieren waarop feministische en queer vormen evolueren, opnieuw verschijnen of meer aspecten kunnen onthullen naarmate ze door verschillende doelgroepen worden opgepakt en geïnterpreteerd. De kunst van Rijk kan gezien worden als een ‘queer vorm.’ Een queer vorm is elke materiële vorm, constructie of patroon dat gearticuleerd is naar of een aspect van gender en seksuele non-conformiteit of divergentie bevat. Daarbij tonen queer vormen ook de verschillende aspecten van gender en seksualiteit, waardoor deze toegankelijk worden voor onze perceptie en uitnodigen tot interpretaties die blijk geven van de veelzijdige dimensies van gender en seksualiteit.

Via een vorm, in dit geval keramiek waarvan een deel afbeeldingen van homo’s heeft, kan een aspect van seksualiteit en gender zichtbaar worden gemaakt en besproken worden, hier de homoseksuele erotiek en een deel van de beeldcultuur van en voor homo’s zoals Rijk die ervaart en tegenkomt, en die hij vervolgens transformeert naar een nieuw medium, een nieuw en ander niveau. Zie bijvoorbeeld Zonder titel (Sebastiaan) , en de afbeelding daarnaast. De man op de foto voldoet aan veel clichés over hoe een homo eruit ‘moet zien.’ Zeer gespierd, harig met een klein zwembroekje. St. Sebastiaan werd veelvuldig gebruikt om mannelijk naakt te verbeelden. De twee werelden komen hier samen om na te denken over de verheerlijking van mannelijk naakt en (voor de hand liggende) perfectie. Door het pad te volgen van transformatie en vernieuwing worden we geholpen om niet te lang te blijven hangen bij potentiële ideologische betekenissen, of “hun waargenomen authenticiteit in het weerspiegelen van de daadwerkelijke ervaringen van seksuele minderheden,” 7 maar kunnen we kijken naar het creatieve vermogen om nieuwe verbindingen te leggen, ideeën en beelden te scheppen waardoor we weer verder kunnen praten met elkaar.

article_text:
From October 22 to December 19, 2026, Villazan hosts Makos. Inside , the first solo exhibition in Spain of the American photographer Christopher Makos . Pilar Giró is the curator and has chosen sixteen images for the occasion, from Andy Warhol to Jean-Michel Basquiat, David Hockney to Salvador Dalí, Mick Jagger to Pedro Almodóvar and Alaska.

A native of Massachusetts, Makos moved to New York around 1970 after years in California..

Warhol in focus

Andy Warhol, whom Makos came to know in the 1970s, has a large share of the selection. It includes images from Altered Image ( Lady Warhol ), a series made in 1981 in which the artist plays along with rouge and wigs.

The Spanish angle

Three names tie the show most directly to the Madrid public: Alaska, Pedro Almodóvar, and Salvador Dalí, all photographed by Makos.

The Madrid presentation is the first opportunity to see his work in a dedicated space in Spain.

Curatorial text by Pilar Giró

Christopher Makos belongs to a generation of photographers for whom the camera, beyond being a tool of observation, was also a way of being in the world. Born in Massachusetts, he built his life between California and New York, and found in photography a language for approaching people, places, and the culture of his time. His arrival in New York in the early 1970s coincided with one of the city’s moments of greatest creative effervescence, when art, music, film, fashion, and nightlife shared spaces, languages, and protagonists. Makos did not contemplate that world from the outside: he was part of it.

The selection of photographs gathered in the exhibition MAKOS. INSIDE distills, without claiming to exhaust it, his dimension as a photographer: his closeness to his subjects, his curiosity, and above all his ability to capture what defines a person and the cultural time surrounding them. Makos has explained that he needs to know the person he photographs, to talk with them, to establish a relationship before pressing the shutter. Hence the naturalness running through so many of his portraits, and the sense of standing before images that, while belonging to a very specific moment, seem to escape it.

Sixteen photographs that move through different territories of his career and make it possible to understand just how far his photography was able to capture a culture in transformation. Among the images appear figures from art, music, fashion, and film: David Hockney, Keith Haring, Jean-Michel Basquiat, Mick Jagger, or Tom Ford, not as a succession of celebrities but as fragments of a single cultural constellation. The exhibition brings together precisely that transversality: disciplines we tend to separate today appear here connected by a shared energy and a shared way of understanding creation.

Andy Warhol inevitably holds a central place. Makos met him in the 1970s, and a relationship of friendship, complicity, and creative exchange developed between them, yielding some of the most recognizable images of his career. In the series Altered Image , also known as Lady Warhol , the portrait becomes a space for experimentation. Warhol appears in makeup and various wigs, deliberately shifting the codes of gender, identity, and representation. These photographs, made in 1981, do not simply document a physical transformation: they make identity something mutable, constructed, and open.

The exhibition also allows us to recognize Makos’s close relationship with the art world. Hockney, Haring, Basquiat, and Warhol appear before his camera without the solemnity that art history would come to bestow on them. Makos photographs them from a closeness that preserves something of the moment before they became icons. Perhaps that is one of the most singular qualities of his work: his photographs do not seem to pursue posterity, and yet they end up building it.

At VILLAZAN, the exhibition also takes on a particular resonance through the images linked to Spain. Salvador Dalí appears as part of that international universe in which the boundaries between art, entertainment, and public persona were blurring. Pedro Almodóvar and Alaska introduce another geography and another generation, but also a kindred sensibility: freedom as an attitude, experimentation with identity, and the will to transform established cultural codes. Their presence broadens the narrative and reminds us that Makos’s eye was never confined to a single scene.

More than documenting his subjects, Makos captured what was happening around them: the intensity of a cultural moment, the relationships between disciplines, the energy of a generation, and a certain idea of freedom. His images were born of the immediate, but have become part of our visual memory. We do not merely recognize those who appear in them; through these photographs, we recognize a way of imagining an entire era.

Perhaps that is why his work retains such a contemporary force today. Makos has the ability to fix the instant without locking it into its time. His vision transforms what is observed into image and the moment into memory; he turns the immediate into something that ends up seeming classic.

Pilar Giró

editorial_excerpt_zh: 杰森·斯坦森主演了不错的动作戏，但剧本安于塑造可预测的角色和阴谋，让一场简单的复仇变得令人疲惫。本文《影评 | 《代码：复仇》（2026）：未充分利用的配方》最初发布于 Cinema com Rapadura 。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "杰森·斯坦森主演了不错的动作戏，但剧本安于塑造可预测的角色和阴谋，让一场简单的复仇变得令人疲惫。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "杰森·斯坦森凭借自身的气场撑起了许多平庸的动作故事，以此构建了其职业生涯，他倚重自己的体魄以及诠释那些能够应对任何对手的硬汉时的自信。然而，《代码：复仇》却过于依赖这种熟悉感，以至于几乎无法将主角与该演员先前的角色区分开来。斯坦森依然极具说服力，但他身边的角色和冲突却在重复这一公式，却没有找到多少可发挥的余地。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这一次的主角是科尔·里德（Cole Reed），一名特种部队退伍军人兼前纽约警察，目前从事司机和私人安保工作。他的雇主在一次伏击中遇害，这让他踏上了涉及一艘贩卖人口船只的复仇之路。这个基础很容易让人联想到“虎胆龙威”（“Duro de Matar”）系列，将一个备战充分的战斗人员与集中在限定空间内的对手结合在了一起。然而，剧本却把本可以很简单的事情搞复杂了，加入了阴谋、背叛和揭秘，却没有对涉事人员进行足够的展开来让这些发现变得有趣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "里德的军事背景及其警察世家的传统，其存在只是为了重申斯坦森的个人气场本就轻易暗示出的能力与原则。这最终并未给主角带来任何实质性能让他区别于该演员那么多其他角色的特质。看到亿万富翁老板的死似乎比贩运受害者的处境更能触动他，这种讽刺感也十分显著（至少可以说）。犯罪更多是用来确立对手的残酷，而复仇则依然局限于对老板失去的哀悼。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其余演员几乎没有获得什么空间来弥补这些局限，这并不令人意外。安娜贝拉·沃利斯（Annabelle Wallis）饰演的角色拥有与其家庭相关的潜力，但由于缺乏足够的展开，最终不过是一个剧本工具。片中还出现了其他可预测的人物，以及缺乏个性且增加了信息量却未能提升冲突兴趣的对话。在战斗之间的间隙，这种脆弱性表现得尤为沉重，而正是在这些时刻，长片恰恰依赖关系和调查来维持注意力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在动作戏中，执行力终于为素材找到了一些力量。导演让-弗朗索瓦·里谢（Jean-François Richet）的履历上有好几部动作电影，包括《亡命救赎》（“Herança de Sangue”）和最近的《飞机扣押》（“Alerta Máximo”）。里谢在清晰地拍摄和剪辑对决、保留打击感以及充分挖掘斯坦森的体能方面表现得很称职。这些动作场面血腥，其中一些堪称该演员近期作品中最令人满意的场景之一。这些时刻表明，只要在制作上用心，老套路也能发挥作用。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种喘息机会的匮乏使得关系的匮乏、调查的匮乏以及所有非战斗环节的失控显得更加沉重。没有必要用95分钟全部填满搏斗，但接连不断的解释和被拉长的场景并未构建起足够的张力，使得这部长片即便片长很短也显得拖沓。对于一部只需要让斯坦森做他最擅长的事情的电影来说，《代码：复仇》连遵循自己的配方都感到吃力。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Jason Statham protagoniza boas cenas de ação, mas o roteiro se acomoda em personagens previsíveis e intrigas que tornam cansativa uma simples vingança.

Jason Statham construiu uma carreira sustentando histórias de ação banais com sua presença, apostando no porte físico e na segurança com que interpreta homens capazes de enfrentar qualquer adversário. “ Código: Vingança ”, porém, depende tanto dessa familiaridade que é praticamente incapaz de distinguir seu protagonista dos personagens anteriores do ator. Statham ainda convence, mas está cercado por personagens e conflitos que repetem a fórmula sem encontrar muito o que fazer com ela.

O protagonista da vez é Cole Reed, um veterano das Forças Especiais e ex-policial de Nova York que trabalha como motorista e segurança particular. O assassinato do seu empregador numa emboscada o coloca em uma busca por vingança que envolve um navio utilizado para o tráfico humano. A base remete bem à franquia “Duro de Matar” , com essa combinação de um homem preparado para o combate e os adversários concentrados em um espaço delimitado. Porém, o roteiro complica o que poderia ser simples, adicionando conspirações, traições e revelações sem desenvolver as pessoas envolvidas o suficiente para tornar as descobertas interessantes.

O passado militar de Reed e sua tradição familiar na polícia existem para reafirmar a competência e os princípios que a própria presença de Statham já sugere com facilidade. Isso acaba não trazendo ao protagonista algo que, de fato, o torne diferente de tantos outros personagens do ator. Também é notável a ironia (para dizer o mínimo) de ver que a morte do chefe bilionário parece mobilizá-lo bem mais do que a situação das vítimas de tráfico. O crime serve muito mais para estabelecer a crueldade dos adversários, enquanto a vingança permanece presa à perda do patrão.

Não é surpresa que o restante do elenco receba pouquíssimo espaço para compensar as limitações. Annabelle Wallis interpreta uma personagem com possibilidades ligadas à sua família, mas sem desenvolvimento suficiente para ser mais que um mecanismo de roteiro. Surgem outras figuras previsíveis, além de diálogos sem muita personalidade que acrescentam informações sem aumentar o interesse pelo conflito. Essa fragilidade pesa ainda mais nos intervalos entre as lutas, quando o longa depende justamente das relações e da investigação para manter a atenção.

Nas cenas de ação, a execução finalmente encontra alguma força no material. O diretor Jean-François Richet conta com vários filmes de ação no currículo, incluindo “Herança de Sangue” e o mais recente “Alerta Máximo” . Richet é competente ao filmar e montar os confrontos com clareza e preservar o impacto dos golpes, além de explorar bem a capacidade física de Statham. As sequências são sangrentas, com algumas figurando entre as mais satisfatórias dos trabalhos recentes do ator. São momentos que demonstram como o clichê pode funcionar quando há cuidado em sua realização.

A escassez desses respiros pesa ainda mais porque as relações, a investigação e tudo o mais que não é luta não funcionam. Não é necessário preencher os 95 minutos com combates, mas as sucessivas explicações e cenas esticadas não constroem tensão suficiente, fazendo o longa parecer arrastado mesmo com a curta duração. Para um filme que precisava apenas deixar Statham fazer o que faz de melhor, “Código: Vingança” sofre até para seguir a própria receita.
